body:
### Description

`presidio-analyzer` 2.2.366 requires `preshed<3.0.14` unconditionally. `preshed` 3.0.13 has no wheel for CPython 3.15, so on 3.15 pip/uv builds it from source, and that build breaks spaCy model loading at runtime. `preshed` 3.0.15 fixes the underlying bug, but the pin keeps it out.

### Steps to reproduce

On CPython 3.15.2, Linux x86_64, with a project depending on `presidio-analyzer==2.2.366`:

```
preshed==3.0.13          # sdist, no cp315 wheel, compiled during install
spacy==3.8.18            # cp315 wheel
```

Then:

```python
import spacy
spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
```

fails with:

```
File "spacy/tokenizer.pyx", line 239, in spacy.tokenizer.Tokenizer._flush_specials
  del self._specials[k]
OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C ssize_t
```

### Expected behavior

`presidio-analyzer` installs and its spaCy-backed NLP engine loads on CPython 3.15.

### Evidence that preshed is the cause

Changing only `preshed`, leaving spaCy and the model identical, fixes it:

| preshed | wheel for 3.15 | `spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")` |
|---|---|---|
| 3.0.13 | no, compiles from sdist | `OverflowError` |
| 3.0.15 | yes | loads fine |

This matches the reports in explosion/spaCy#14058, where the same traceback appears on 3.13 and 3.14 with `preshed` 3.0.14 and disappears with 3.0.15. My own PII-removal test suite (presidio analyzer plus anonymizer) passes on 3.15 once `preshed` is 3.0.15.

### What I would like

Relax the pin so consumers can take a working `preshed`, for example `preshed>=3.0.2,<3.1.0`. Keeping `<3.0.14` means anything on Python 3.15 is forced onto a source build that does not work, and works around it only with dependency overrides.

comments.body:
Related pin in the same release: `presidio-analyzer` 2.2.366 also requires `numpy<2.5.0`.

`numpy` 2.4.6 has no cp315 wheel, so on Python 3.15 that cap forces a source build of numpy too, which means a C toolchain in every downstream image. `numpy` 2.5.x ships the wheel, and the packages around it here accept it (`numba` 0.68 allows `<2.6`, `scipy` 1.17 allows `<2.7`, `thinc` 8.3 allows `<3`), so it looks like the cap could move with them.

title: preshed<3.0.14 pins consumers to a broken build on Python 3.15
